source: DeFi exploits on chains outside the Solana + EVM scope covered by the two main datasets. Covers verifiable major incidents on Sui, Cosmos ecosystem, NEAR, Aptos, Polkadot parachains, and other non-EVM non-Solana L1s. Excludes CEX-adjacent incidents, tokens/wallets unrelated to smart-contract protocols, and unverified or anonymous reports. Intended for the combined 'all tracked DeFi' view; the chain-level Solana vs EVM comparison does not include these entries.

hacks.rootCause: Integer overflow in shared math library (checked_shlw function) combined with spoofed fake-token attack on concentrated liquidity pools. Attacker exploited flaws in the largest DEX aggregator on Sui, draining approximately $220-260M from liquidity pools
hacks.recoveryNote: Sui validators froze approximately $162M in stolen funds via chain-level intervention; attacker offered a $6M bounty for asset recovery; Cetus relaunched 17 days after the exploit

hacks.rootCause: Misconfiguration of the newly deployed iBTC/aUSD liquidity pool allowed the attacker to mint approximately 1.28B aUSD stablecoin tokens without adequate collateral. aUSD depegged dramatically, losing 99% of value
hacks.recoveryNote: Acala paused network trades via urgent governance vote, disabled aUSD transfer functions, identified 16 addresses holding erroneously minted tokens, and burned the unbacked supply via on-chain governance. Net realised user loss substantially smaller than the gross mint figure

hacks.rootCause: Money market exploit via a Move contract vulnerability. Attacker drained user deposits from Thala's lending product on Aptos
hacks.recoveryNote: Aptos ecosystem response included coordinated asset freezes; partial fund recovery via post-incident negotiations

hacks.rootCause: Oracle manipulation via 423 fake wallets inflating liquidity pool prices to borrow against artificial collateral. Rhea Finance was formed in early 2025 through the merger of Ref Finance and Burrow Finance
hacks.recoveryNote: Tether froze approximately $3M of stolen assets; protocol implemented emergency oracle fix

hacks.rootCause: Protocol logic bug in a Move contract managing vault deposits
hacks.recoveryNote: No recovery at time of disclosure

hacks.rootCause: Yield market pool drain exploited via Move contract vulnerability during pre-maintenance window
hacks.recoveryNote: Incident investigated by Halborn; limited recovery

hacks.rootCause: MMR (Merkle Mountain Range) proof verifier bug allowed forged cross-chain messages. Attacker minted unbacked cross-chain tokens by submitting fraudulent proofs
hacks.recoveryNote: Emergency pause of affected bridge routes; recovery status unclear

hacks.rootCause: Critical bug in liquidity pool mechanism allowed adding liquidity and immediately withdrawing a larger amount than deposited. Vulnerability detected and the blockchain halted at block 4713065 to prevent further losses
hacks.recoveryNote: Chain halt and restart on June 13 2022 with fix applied; some funds recovered through voluntary returns and bounty

hacks.rootCause: Bifrost ETH router exploit: custom wrapper contracts tricked the cross-chain Bifrost into recognising phantom deposits. Attacker minted synthetic assets without collateral
hacks.recoveryNote: Post-incident audits and code freeze; some funds lost permanently

hacks.rootCause: ETH router override loop (designed only for vault transfer incidents) was manipulated via a custom wrapper contract to access the override function
hacks.recoveryNote: Second exploit within a week of the July 16 incident; protocol paused and rewrote router contracts
